mfg1-electrical-l071.title: Intrinsic, n-type, p-type, and the pn junction
mfg1-electrical-l071.objective: Understand a pn junction by separating impurities, carriers, and the internal field.

paragraphs.title: Atomic bonds and impurities
paragraphs.text: Silicon and germanium are representative intrinsic semiconductors. Adding a small amount of suitable impurity to silicon changes carrier behavior. Electrons are majority carriers in n-type material and holes in p-type; n/p does not simply mean the whole material has negative/positive charge.

paragraphs.title: Donors and acceptors
paragraphs.text: Adding a five-valence-electron atom such as phosphorus to silicon is a donor example; a three-valence-electron atom such as boron is an acceptor example. A hole represents a missing electron; movement of surrounding electrons allows us to describe the hole as moving.

paragraphs.title: At the junction
paragraphs.text: Joining p-type and n-type material causes carrier diffusion and recombination near the boundary, forming a depletion layer with few mobile majority carriers and an internal electric field. It is not an empty physical gap or a region without fixed charges. The external voltage direction changes junction behavior.

terms.meaning: Outer electrons involved in atomic bonding and similar interactions.
Electrons or holes carrying current.
A region near the junction with fewer mobile majority carriers.
Electrons and holes combining and ceasing to act as carriers.

mfg1-electrical-l071.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Compare intrinsic, n-type, and p-type material by carriers and impurities. Explain hole movement and the depletion layer using words on a diagram.
safety: Do not energize components with unknown polarity or ratings based on semiconductor explanations.
mfg1-electrical-l071.summary: Understand a pn junction by separating impurities, carriers, and the internal field.

mfg1-electrical-l072.title: FETs, IGBTs, and IC function groups
mfg1-electrical-l072.objective: Separate device control, characteristics, and limits from IC functions.

paragraphs.title: Three terminals do not imply the same roles
paragraphs.text: Unlike a bipolar transistor’s B/C/E, a FET uses gate-based electric-field control. An IGBT is a power device with an insulated gate. Consult model documents for terminal names, drive conditions, maximum ratings, and static sensitivity; identical shape does not establish interchangeability.

paragraphs.title: Separate characteristics from ratings
paragraphs.text: hFE, switching time, and saturation voltage are characteristics dependent on operating conditions. Maximum current, voltage, and dissipation ratings are limits not to exceed. One favorable characteristic does not establish suitability.

paragraphs.title: Signals and processing
paragraphs.text: Op-amps, A/D, D/A, regulators, logic, memory, and MPUs have different functions. Modulation reflects an information signal into carrier amplitude, frequency, or phase; demodulation retrieves it. Do not confuse amplification, oscillation, and power stabilization as one process.

terms.meaning: A transistor controlling current through the field effect.
A bipolar power device with an insulated gate.
A terminal-voltage characteristic remaining under specified on-state conditions or similar conditions.
A microprocessor handling calculation, control, and similar tasks.

mfg1-electrical-l072.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Make a role diagram from sensor to MPU. Explain document checks for a FET gate versus BJT base and the distinction between characteristics and maximum ratings.
safety: Do not replace a different device type merely because the terminal count matches.
mfg1-electrical-l072.summary: Separate device control, characteristics, and limits from IC functions.

mfg1-electrical-l073.title: Analog scales, clamp meters, and measurement error
mfg1-electrical-l073.objective: Match range, function, and effects on the circuit before measuring.

paragraphs.title: Combine range and scale
paragraphs.text: Read an analog meter using the selected range and corresponding scale. A reading of 20 on a 50 full-scale scale with a 25 mA range is 10 mA. Resistance scales are nonlinear and use multipliers; check zero adjustment for each range. Align the pointer with its mirror image to reduce parallax.

paragraphs.title: Check each model’s capabilities
paragraphs.text: Some DMMs directly measure AC current; do not claim all testers cannot. A clamp meter detects current around a conductor: check method, AC/DC capability, which conductor to enclose, and ratings. Current alone does not directly establish power consumption.

paragraphs.title: Effects on the circuit
paragraphs.text: In the R=V/I voltage-drop method, leads, contacts, and instrument resistance affect the result. Voltmeter input and ammeter insertion also change the circuit, so the display is not automatically the true value. Check oscilloscope bandwidth, sample rate, memory, and probe conditions too.

terms.meaning: A reading shift caused by viewing from a different position.
A current meter with a sensing section enclosing a conductor.

terms.reading: にゅうりょくていこう
terms.meaning: Resistance presented at an instrument’s input.
The number of signal acquisitions per unit time.

mfg1-electrical-l073.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Find the reading for full-scale 100, a 5 V range, and an indication of 64. Explain lead resistance in resistance measurements and input resistance in voltage measurements.
safety: Attach clamps or probes only within assigned procedures, ratings, and safe conditions.
mfg1-electrical-l073.summary: Match range, function, and effects on the circuit before measuring.

mfg1-electrical-l074.title: Tidy up and hand over after assembly
mfg1-electrical-l074.objective: Tidying is a process of checking quantities, foreign material, and status before handover.

paragraphs.title: Preparation and fatigue
paragraphs.text: Prepare clothing, tools, parts, work surfaces, lighting, instructions, static protection, ventilation, and cooling. Familiar prolonged work can reduce attention through fatigue; follow workplace break plans. Match protection to hazards and avoid items that may be caught in rotation.

paragraphs.title: Restore quantities and condition
paragraphs.text: Return tools, remaining parts, and documents to designated locations and remove solder scraps and offcuts using specified tools. Check for foreign material inside boards or housings and distinguish held from good items. Do not leave everything simply assuming the next worker will do the same job.

paragraphs.title: Records for the next decision
paragraphs.text: Record part number, lot, quantity, completed scope, unfinished work, machine condition, abnormalities and actions, and recipient. If remaining counts disagree, report possible mixing or shortages instead of forcing the numbers to balance. Continue isolation and residual-heat precautions during cleaning.

terms.meaning: Passing status and necessary information to the next responsible person.
Something not intended to be present in a product or process.
The quantity left after use or processing.
An item held separately pending a decision or action.

mfg1-electrical-l074.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Write an end-of-work record for 32 planned items:25 complete,2 held, and 5 not started. Prepare a handover message about one missing tool.
safety: Do not reach into running machinery to clean or recover tools.
mfg1-electrical-l074.summary: Tidying is a process of checking quantities, foreign material, and status before handover.

mfg1-electrical-l075.title: Verify logic laws with truth tables
mfg1-electrical-l075.objective: Specify operators and the scope of negation, and check all input combinations.

paragraphs.title: Order within the same operation
paragraphs.text: In binary logic, +means OR, ·means AND, and NOT means negation. Commutative and associative laws allow order or parentheses to change within the same operator without changing results. Unlike ordinary arithmetic, x+x=x and x·x=x.

paragraphs.title: Zero, one, and negation
paragraphs.text: x+0=x, x·1=x, x+1=1, and x·0=0. Also x+NOT x=1, x·NOT x=0, and double negation returns x. Check absorption x+x·y=x and distribution x·(y+z)=x·y+x·z through four or eight input combinations.

paragraphs.title: What is negated
paragraphs.text: De Morgan gives NOT(x+y)=(NOT x)·(NOT y) and NOT(x·y)=(NOT x)+(NOT y). Use parentheses to identify negation scope. Simplifying a logic expression does not replace evaluation of failure behavior or safety.

terms.meaning: A table listing input combinations and their logical results.
A logic law that simplifies overlapping conditions.
A law expanding an operation into or out of parentheses.
Applying negation twice returns the original value.

mfg1-electrical-l075.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Make a four-row table for x+x·y. Give one input at which NOT(x+y) differs from NOT x+NOT y.
safety: Do not approve safety-circuit changes merely because logic expressions are equivalent.
mfg1-electrical-l075.summary: Specify operators and the scope of negation, and check all input combinations.

mfg1-electrical-l076.title: Switches, sensors, relays, and SSRs
mfg1-electrical-l076.objective: Separate detection principles from output methods when identifying parts.

paragraphs.title: Components creating inputs
paragraphs.text: Pushbuttons can return automatically or retain state. A mechanical limit switch changes contacts through object movement; photoelectric and proximity sensors use different detection principles. For float and pressure detection too, consult specifications for the measured quantity and output form.

paragraphs.title: Switching through electromagnetism
paragraphs.text: An electromagnetic relay moves a mechanism and contacts with coil-generated magnetic force. A contactor switches larger loads but may not itself contain short-circuit or overcurrent protection. Match coil rating, contact capacity, a/b arrangement, and device identifier.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish semiconductor outputs
paragraphs.text: SSRs mainly switch through semiconductors, so not all relays can be explained as mechanical contacts and coils. Check off-state leakage, heating, and load requirements. The shape or contacts of an emergency stop alone do not certify the equipment’s whole safety function.

terms.meaning: A switch changing contacts according to object position or movement.
A device opening and closing a load circuit through electromagnetic force.
A relay using semiconductors for switching.
Returning to the original state when the action is released.

mfg1-electrical-l076.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Compare inputs, operating principles, and ratings for pushbuttons, position sensors, electromagnetic relays, and SSRs. Report non-detection without independently changing wiring.
safety: Do not bypass sensor or emergency-stop signals to make machinery operate.
mfg1-electrical-l076.summary: Separate detection principles from output methods when identifying parts.

mfg1-electrical-l077.title: State changes of thermal relays and timers
mfg1-electrical-l077.objective: Separate overload detection, main-circuit switching, and timing.

paragraphs.title: Detecting overload
paragraphs.text: A thermal relay detects overload using heating from overcurrent and components such as bimetal strips. A bimetal combines metals with different thermal expansion. Do not assume it alone interrupts the main circuit; it is normally combined with a contactor.

paragraphs.title: Delaying on
paragraphs.text: A basic on-delay turns the output on after the set time from input-on, and turns it off when the input goes off. In the basic example, an input shorter than the setting produces no output. Check each contact for timed operation and instantaneous return.

paragraphs.title: Delaying off
paragraphs.text: A basic off-delay turns on with the input, then off after the set delay from input-off. Retention and power conditions differ by product; do not assume identical behavior on loss of supply. Draw separate input/output lines against time to verify.

terms.meaning: A relay using heat to detect overload.
A bonded material made from metals with different thermal expansion.
An action delaying output-on after input-on.
An action delaying output-off after input-off.

mfg1-electrical-l077.activity:
30-minute study target: reading 10 minutes, organizing examples 8, writing 9, reflection 3.
Explain the output for a 3-second basic on-delay receiving 2-second and 5-second inputs. Compare the output timing after the input ends for an off-delay.
safety: Do not ignore protection trips when resetting or changing timer settings.
mfg1-electrical-l077.summary: Separate overload detection, main-circuit switching, and timing.
